question: The Chinese Government has been known to use economic coercion as a means of leverage. A prominent example of this in the EU was the case of Lithuania. My office has received information relating to individual cases where there have been restrictions on the supply of products from China to Germany. The supplier explained that no orders could currently be placed from Germany and France. 1.
What information does the Commission have about possible supply restrictions from China to France, Germany and other Member States?
Is the Commission aware of similar cases in the aforementioned or other Member States?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.3.2024) The Commission is not aware of the restrictions mentioned by the Honourable Member concerning the supply of products from China to Germany and France or other Member States. However, the Commission will get in touch with the Honourable Member’s office to obtain more details on the products concerned that allegedly are subject to supply restrictions.
